findings.summary: Page 2 opens with a `git worktree add` recipe two pages before worktrees are introduced or defined anywhere.
findings.evidence: First block of page 2: `git worktree add -b hotfix-501 \ ../hotfix origin/main` / `# fix, test, push` / `git worktree remove ../hotfix` — while the worktree concept is first defined on page 4 ("Your First Worktree", "Second directory, same `.git` object database").
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 2 (the same hotfix recipe already appears in context on page 9 under "Worked Example: Hot Build"), so page 2 begins with its actual heading "Look Before You Restore".

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with an unheaded dropped-stash recovery recipe that uses `apply`, dropping, and unreachable objects before any of them are taught.
findings.evidence: Final block of page 1: `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` / `git show <sha>` / `git stash apply <sha>` — but `git stash apply` and `drop` are first defined on page 2's "Restore, Keep Or Kill" table, and unreachable/gc recovery on pages 2–3 ("Stash commits are unreachable from any branch", "Recover A Dropped Stash").
findings.fix: Remove this block from page 1 — page 3 already carries it under the "Recover A Dropped Stash" heading — and let page 1 end on the "Your First Stash" bullets.

findings.summary: The stated garbage-collection window for stash commits names the wrong config knob and the wrong default, and wrongly implies live stack entries are gc candidates.
findings.evidence: "Stash commits are unreachable from any branch / So they are garbage-collection candidates / Window = `gc.reflogExpireUnreachable`, 30 days"
findings.fix: Replace with: entries still on the stack are protected by the `refs/stash` reflog, which Git special-cases to never expire by default (`reflog.c`: "If unconfigured, make stash never expire"). Once an entry is dropped its commit becomes unreachable and survives only until `git gc` prunes it — the governing knob is `gc.pruneExpire`, default `2.weeks.ago`, not `gc.reflogExpireUnreachable`.

findings.summary: Tells scripts to detect a no-op stash via exit status, but `git stash push` exits 0 when there is nothing to save.
findings.evidence: "No changes: 'No local changes to save' / Nothing pushed — check exit status in scripts"
findings.fix: State that the exit status is 0 in this case (`do_push_stash` prints the message and returns `ret`, still 0), so scripts must detect it another way — compare `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/stash` before and after, or use `git stash create` and test for empty output.

findings.summary: Page 4 tells the reader `--force` overrides "the hard rule" without ever stating what that rule is; it is only defined on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 closing bullets: "`--force` overrides the hard rule", "Then two indexes race on one ref" — the rule itself appears on page 5 under "One Branch, One Tree": "fatal: 'main' is already checked out at '/repo'".
findings.fix: Move these three `--force` bullets to page 5, directly after the "One Branch, One Tree" code block, or restate the rule inline on page 4 ("the same branch cannot be checked out in two worktrees") before mentioning the override.

findings.summary: Claims a force-delete of a branch held by a linked worktree succeeds and leaves an orphan ref, but Git blocks the deletion unconditionally.
findings.evidence: "Deleting a branch a linked worktree holds is blocked / Force-deleting leaves that worktree on an orphan ref"
findings.fix: Correct to: `git branch -D` is blocked too — the worktree check in `builtin/branch.c` is not gated on `--force` and always errors with "Cannot delete branch 'x' used by worktree at '<path>'". The fix is to `git worktree remove <path>` (or switch that worktree to another branch) first, then delete.

findings.summary: Describes `--staged` as the exact mirror of `--keep-index`, which misstates what `--keep-index` puts into the stash entry.
findings.evidence: "Git 2.35+: stashes only staged changes / Unstaged work stays in the tree untouched / Exactly the mirror of `--keep-index`"
findings.fix: Drop "exactly" and clarify the asymmetry: `--keep-index` stashes staged *and* unstaged changes and merely restores the index content to the working tree, whereas `--staged` puts only the staged changes into the entry. (Same issue with the label `git stash push -k -m "unstaged rest"` — the entry holds more than the unstaged rest.)

findings.summary: Says a branch switch destroys ignored build directories, contradicting the deck's own statement that a switch leaves ignored files alone.
findings.evidence: "10-minute build: switching kills `node_modules`" — versus page 1: "Untracked and ignored files / Branch switch ignores them ... They survive the switch"
findings.fix: Reword to what actually happens: a switch leaves `node_modules/`, `target/` and `__pycache__/` on disk untouched, but a changed lockfile or changed sources invalidate them, forcing a reinstall or full rebuild.

findings.summary: Understates stash storage as one commit per entry, contradicting the deck's own 2-or-3-parent model.
findings.evidence: "One commit + trees + blobs per stash entry"
findings.fix: Change to "Two commits per entry (working tree + index), three with `-u`" — the index and untracked parents are themselves commits, as the page 2 anatomy diagram states.

findings.summary: The quoted `git worktree list` output uses a label and paths Git does not print.
findings.fix: Git prints `(detached HEAD)`, not `(detached)`, and prints absolute resolved paths rather than `/repo/../rev`. Update the sample to e.g. `/work/rev  4c0de1a (detached HEAD)` and fix the bullet to say `(detached HEAD)`. Optionally note that stale rows are annotated `prunable`.

findings.summary: Repeats the wrong recovery window for dropped stash entries on the final-recall page.
findings.evidence: "Dropped entries survive the gc window, ~30 days"
findings.fix: Change to "~2 weeks (`gc.pruneExpire`, default `2.weeks.ago`)" to match the actual prune grace period for unreachable objects.

findings.summary: The scripting recipe applies an unset `$sha`, so the final command runs against an empty argument.
findings.evidence: "git stash list --format='%H %gs' |", "  grep -F \"$tag\"   # find the SHA", "git stash apply \"$sha\"  # not pop"
findings.fix: Capture the hash: `sha=$(git stash list --format='%H %gs' | grep -F "$tag" | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1)` before `git stash apply "$sha"`.

findings.summary: The scripting example applies `$sha`, a variable the snippet never assigns.
findings.evidence: Page 10: `git stash list --format='%H %gs' |` / `  grep -F "$tag"   # find the SHA` / `git stash apply "$sha"  # not pop` — the grep only prints; `$sha` is unset when applied.
findings.fix: Capture the value: `sha=$(git stash list --format='%H %gs' | grep -F "$tag" | cut -d' ' -f1)` then `git stash apply "$sha"`.
